question: What defines a communicable disease?

options.A: Physiological failure due to environmental mineral toxicity
options.B: Genetic mutations inherited directly from maternal lineages
options.C: Illnesses transmitted from a reservoir to a susceptible host
options.D: Degenerative cellular breakdown of body tissues over time

explanation: Communicable diseases require an infectious agent that can spread from an infected source to a new host, differentiating them from non-communicable chronic illnesses. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why is the public health perspective fundamentally different from individual clinical care?

options.A: It prioritizes community-wide protection over single-patient diagnosis
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for pharmaceutical interventions
options.C: It focuses exclusively on surgical correction of congenital defects
options.D: It ignores epidemiological data in favor of traditional remedies

explanation: While clinical nursing focuses on healing the person in front of you, public health looks at population-level patterns to protect the broader community. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h1)

question: What are the three core elements of the epidemiological triangle?
explanation: The classic epidemiological triangle consists of the agent that infects, the host that carries it, and the environment that brings them together. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h2)

question: How does handwashing interrupt the chain of infection?

options.A: By altering the genetic makeup of the host
options.B: By increasing the virulence of the pathogen
options.C: By disrupting the mode of transmission
options.D: By destroying the natural environment completely

explanation: Physical removal of pathogens from hands stops the agent from traveling between surfaces and susceptible hosts. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h2)

question: Which activity represents primary prevention?

options.A: Providing physical therapy after a stroke

explanation: Primary prevention prevents the initial occurrence of a disease, and vaccination is a classic example of this level. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h3)

question: A community health nurse sets up a screening camp for early detection of hypertension. Which level of prevention does this address?
explanation: Screening aims to detect disease early in asymptomatic individuals so treatment can begin before complications develop, defining secondary prevention. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of public health disease surveillance?

options.A: Systematic collection and analysis of health data to guide action
options.B: Punishing healthcare facilities that fail to maintain cleanliness
options.C: Billing insurance companies for infectious disease treatments
options.D: Conducting clinical drug trials for pharmaceutical corporations

explanation: Surveillance tracks disease trends over time so public health agencies can allocate resources and stop outbreaks early. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why is immediate notification of epidemic-prone diseases legally required in clinical practice?

options.A: To ensure automatic financial compensation for patients
options.B: To trigger rapid public health containment measures
options.C: To bypass the need for laboratory confirmation testing
options.D: To mandate immediate patient discharge from the hospital

explanation: Early notification gives health ministries the vital time needed to mobilize response teams before localized cases explode into widespread community transmission. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is the key difference between isolation and quarantine?

options.A: Quarantine is permanent, whereas isolation lasts for exactly twenty-four hours
options.B: Quarantine applies only to hospital staff, while isolation applies to visitors
options.C: Isolation separates infected persons, while quarantine restricts exposed healthy persons
options.D: Isolation uses chemical disinfectants, while quarantine relies on thermal barriers

explanation: Isolation deals with those who are actively sick to protect others, whereas quarantine monitors those who were exposed but do not yet show symptoms. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which of the following practices is mandated under standard precautions?

options.A: Skipping hand hygiene if gloves appear visibly clean
options.B: Isolating every patient who enters a surgical ward
options.C: Wearing full biohazard suits for every routine bed bath
options.D: Treating all body fluids as potentially infectious for every patient

explanation: Standard precautions assume every patient's blood, non-intact skin, mucous membranes, and moist body substances carry pathogens, regardless of diagnosis. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h5)

question: How does herd immunity protect a community?

options.A: By administering massive doses of antibiotics to every newborn child
options.B: By immunizing a high percentage of the population to block transmission pathways
options.C: By quarantining entire cities at the first sign of a viral mutation
options.D: By eliminating all animal reservoirs of disease within a given region

explanation: When enough people are immune, the chain of transmission breaks down, indirectly shielding unimmunized or immunocompromised community members. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of administering chemoprophylaxis to an exposed individual?

options.A: To prevent an established exposure from developing into active disease
options.B: To replace the need for active immunization schedules entirely
options.C: To permanently alter human DNA to resist future infections
options.D: To cure a chronic autoimmune condition over a long period

explanation: Chemoprophylaxis uses prophylactic drugs to suppress or kill pathogens before they multiply enough to cause clinical illness. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h6)

question: Which intervention directly targets vector-borne diseases like malaria?

options.A: Boiling all municipal drinking water supplies
options.B: Administering standard precautions in surgical theaters
options.D: Isolating infected patients in negative pressure rooms

explanation: Mosquito nets physically block and kill the vector responsible for transmitting the malaria parasite to humans. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h7)

question: Why are clean water and proper sewage disposal critical for controlling typhoid fever?

options.A: They prevent the fecal-oral transmission cycle of the pathogen
options.B: They destroy the respiratory system of airborne viral agents
options.C: They stimulate active herd immunity within the population
options.D: They eliminate animal vectors like rodents and bats

explanation: Typhoid spreads when contaminated human waste enters drinking water or food sources, making sanitation essential for interruption. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h7)

question: What event signals the need for a formal outbreak investigation?

options.A: A single patient is diagnosed with a common viral upper respiratory infection
options.B: Disease incidence exceeds normal baseline expectancy in a community
options.C: A hospital nurse notices a minor inventory shortage of surgical gloves
options.D: Routine annual budget allocations are finalized by the health ministry

explanation: An outbreak is defined by an unusual clustering or surge of cases above what is normally expected for that time and place. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h8)

question: What is the purpose of establishing a clear case definition during an active outbreak investigation?

options.A: To prevent the media from reporting on the public health crisis
options.B: To ensure all investigators identify and count cases using identical criteria
options.C: To replace laboratory diagnostic testing with clinical guesswork
options.D: To automatically mandate immediate surgical intervention for every patient

explanation: Standardized case definitions ensure data consistency so epidemiologists can accurately track the scope and spread of the outbreak. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h8)

question: What is the primary goal of community health promotion in communicable disease control?

options.A: Enforcing strict legal penalties for missing medical appointments
options.B: Replacing professional nursing care with home remedies entirely
options.C: Empowering individuals with knowledge to adopt healthy behaviors
options.D: Eliminating the need for epidemiological surveillance systems

explanation: Health promotion equips people with the understanding and tools needed to protect themselves and their families from preventable diseases. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h9)

question: Why is addressing cultural beliefs and stigmas crucial during health education campaigns?

options.A: It stops vector breeding cycles in stagnant community water pools
options.B: It completely replaces the need for environmental sanitation efforts
options.C: It encourages early healthcare-seeking behavior and reduces concealment
options.D: It guarantees that pharmaceutical companies will donate free medications

explanation: When fear and stigma are replaced with understanding, patients seek medical care sooner, improving outcomes and reducing disease spread. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h9)
